_comment: What this sample pins, and why each pin is here.
OpenShell publishes a Helm chart and images for every commit on main, and separately
for each release tag. This sample pins the v0.1.6 release: a release tag stays
published, where a per-commit 0.0.0-dev.<sha> tag is a build artifact that can be
collected later and would leave a reader unable to run the page.
upstream_revision is the commit v0.1.6 points at, recorded so the policy schema and
the pod the driver generates can be read at exactly the version that ran.
A release also publishes the operator CLI as a static binary, so this sample downloads
and verifies it rather than compiling it. cli_sha256 is the value from the release's
own openshell-checksums-sha256.txt. The CLI, the chart, the gateway, the supervisor
and the in-pod runtime therefore all come from one release.
The chart is pinned by version and by the SHA-256 of the archive Helm pulls, and the
three images by digest, so what runs cannot change under a retagged repository.
scripts/setup.sh refuses the chart and the CLI on a checksum mismatch.
